title: Context Budgets: Relevance Over Volume
objective: After this lesson you will be able to budget context by relevance (not volume), estimate token costs with the chars/4 heuristic, dedupe and order context for recency/primacy effects, and cut context deliberately when over budget.
why: 'Just paste the whole manual' works until it doesn't: costs scale linearly, latency climbs, relevant facts drown among irrelevant ones (lost-in-the-middle), and stale context contradicts fresh. Production prompting is an economics of attention — every token must justify itself, and this lesson is the accounting.

blocks.text: Estimate first: **≈1 token per 4 characters** of English prose (code/Unicode denser). A 20,000-character manual ≈ 5,000 tokens; at $X/1K input tokens, each call costs 5X — times thousands of calls. Budgets follow: reserve ~60% for retrieved/task content, ~20% instructions + examples, ~20% headroom for output. Estimates precede structures: measure with the counter before designing what fits.

blocks.caption: Estimate before structuring: parts, totals, flags, projected spend

blocks.text: Context quality beats quantity: rank candidate passages by relevance (keyword overlap, recency, source authority) and include top-k only. Three ranking rules: **recency** (fresh policy supersedes — order newest last for recency weight, Ch.4), **authority** (policy text outranks forum quotes — label sources), **diversity** (three perspectives beat three paraphrases of one — dedupe near-duplicates by overlap).
Lost in the middle: position effects

Models attend unevenly: **primacy** (early content) and **recency** (late content) dominate; middles blur. Exploit deliberately: instructions first (primacy for rules), the decisive evidence last (recency for judgment), supporting detail in the middle. Never bury the one critical constraint mid-prompt — position is a control surface, not an accident.

blocks.caption: Floor, rank, dedupe, cap — relevance pipeline in twelve lines

blocks.title: Spend the budget
blocks.note: Run it: expect picked [policy-v3, ticket] with used 1600 (forum-quote's 2000 exceeds remaining 400 — skipped, and old-policy never reached). Budget caps are ruthless by design: rank well, because the cap keeps only the head.

items: Estimate with chars/4 before structuring; budget ~60/20/20 content/instructions/headroom
Rank by relevance/recency/authority/diversity — include top-k, never dumps
Position deliberately: rules first (primacy), decisive evidence last (recency), support middle
Hard caps with dedupe; stale context contradicts fresh — version and prefer recency

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice assembler and explain why forum-quote is skipped (remaining budget math). (b) Reorder passages by a relevance ranking of your design (policy-v3 0.9, ticket 0.95, forum 0.3, old-v1 0.1, floor 0.2) and state the picked set under a 2000-char cap. (c) State where the decisive return-policy sentence goes (first/middle/last) and why.
hints: Skipped math: 2000 − 1200 − 400 = 400 remaining < 2000 needed → break (hard cap, no partials). Old-v1 never evaluated.
Ranked: ticket (0.95), policy-v3 (0.9), forum (0.3); old-v1 (0.1) below floor 0.2 → dropped. Cap 2000: ticket 400 + policy 1200 = 1600, forum needs 2000 > 400 left → picked [ticket, policy-v3].
Decisive sentence last (recency for judgment); rules first (primacy); support middle. Position is control.
exercise.why: Budget mechanics (floors, caps, ordering) are resource allocation, the chapter's real skill: every token justified, stale excluded, decisive positioned. The math is simple; the discipline of applying it is the lesson.

quiz.q: 'Paste the whole 200-page manual' as context. Problems?
options: Linear cost + latency, lost-in-the-middle dilution, stale contradictions — budget by relevance with floors, caps, and recency ordering
quiz.explain: Volume taxes money, speed, and attention simultaneously. Relevance-ranked top-k with versioning beats dumps on all three axes.

quiz.q: One critical constraint must survive. Position?
options: First (rules/primacy) or last (decisive/recency) — never buried mid-prompt where attention blurs
quiz.explain: Attention is U-shaped: primacy and recency dominate. Critical content goes where attention lives; middles hold supporting detail.

quiz.q: Old policy v1 vs new v3 both retrieved. Handling?
options: Version, prefer recency, and label authority — stale context contradicts fresh; undated contradiction resolves randomly
quiz.explain: Contradiction without versioning is a coin flip. Recency preference + source labels let the model (and reviewers) resolve correctly.

summary: Estimate (chars/4), budget (60/20/20), rank (relevance/recency/authority/diversity), position (rules first, evidence last), cap hard. Attention is money — spend it deliberately.
next: Fitted and measured — now face the failure modes honestly: hallucination accommodation, verification patterns, and calibrated trust. Next: failing gracefully.
